title: Current model family selection matrix
summary: Explains why the available evidence does not support a current model-family recommendation and identifies what must be recovered before the matrix can be corrected safely. It prevents unsupported selections while preserving the requirements for a correction-only update.
prerequisites: The source review record that triggered the correction
First-party evidence supporting each model-family claim

sections.title: Which model family should I select?
paragraphs: UNKNOWN. The supplied evidence does not establish any current model-family names, capabilities, constraints, availability, or recommendations, so no model family can be recommended or included in a selection matrix.

This is an intermediate-level decision resource for practitioners. Before making a selection, recover the existing matrix and obtain current first-party evidence for every option and decision rule. If either is unavailable, stop rather than substituting an unsupported recommendation.

sections.title: Correction status and next actions
paragraphs: Changed cited source: UNKNOWN. The only recorded citation is the local path content/resources/model-provider-decisions/current-model-family-selection-matrix.json, with an unregistered publisher and no prior verification. The supplied change record does not establish whether a source moved, exceeded its review cadence, or both. Affected content: UNKNOWN. No source-dependent claim can be corrected safely until the former source, replacement source if any, and affected claims are identified.

First, retrieve the complete baseline resource verbatim. If it cannot be retrieved, request the file or a repository permalink and do not replace its contents. Second, obtain the review event, former source location, replacement location if applicable, publisher, and verification dates. If the event record is incomplete, return it for source review instead of inferring what changed.

Third, check each affected claim against a directly accessible first-party HTTPS source. If a source does not resolve or does not support the claim, omit the claim and request authoritative evidence. Fourth, change only the claims affected by the documented source event. If affected and unaffected text cannot be distinguished, stop and obtain editorial review rather than rewriting the resource.

Finally, compare the corrected file with the recovered baseline. If the comparison contains unrelated wording, ordering, metadata, or formatting changes, restore those lines and repeat the comparison. The official comparison documentation listed in the sources describes examining differences between file or repository states.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is the verbatim baseline, a review record identifying the changed source and trigger, a resolvable first-party HTTPS source for every retained or corrected model-family claim, and a claim-level record of what the source change affected.

Verify the result by comparing the corrected resource with the baseline. A successful correction changes only the affected citation records, verification dates, and claims documented by the source review. If the comparison shows other changes, restore the unaffected material. If the required evidence remains unavailable, the result is not verified and the model-family recommendation remains UNKNOWN.
